topic: Charge of income from house property
question: State the conditions that must be satisfied for income to be taxed under the head 'Income from house property' under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
sources: Income-tax Act, 1961 - section 22 income from house property

points.label: Buildings or lands appurtenant
points.description: The property must be a building or land attached to a building (such as a compound, garage or courtyard); income from vacant land is not taxed under this head.

points.label: Ownership
points.description: The assessee must be the owner, including a deemed owner such as a person who transfers property to a spouse without adequate consideration (other than under an agreement to live apart) or to a minor child (other than a married daughter); the actual owner is taxed even if someone else collects the rent.

points.label: Not used for own business
points.description: The part of the property used by the owner for his own business or profession, the profits of which are taxable, is not taxed under this head.

points.label: Basis is annual value
points.description: Tax is on the annual value of the property, which is a notional figure; it is taxed even if the property is not let out, subject to the rules for self-occupied and vacant property.

points.label: Sub-letting
points.description: Rent received by a tenant from sub-letting is not taxed under this head because the tenant is not the owner; it is taxed as income from other sources or as business income.
